pr_comments: A command returning a 150MB file now takes less than 60ms to resolve. Previously: almost 50 seconds.
Also needs #4752 to fix the unit tests.
We'll detect and use the custom protocol IPC on Linux if available when https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/pull/969 lands. On older webkit2gtk, we'll need to stick with the current approach (JSON :( )

Updates on the 150mb command response benchmark:
macOS: 70-80ms
Linux: 1.3-1.5s (ipc.postMessage), 1.3-1.4s (custom protocol)
Windows: 1.8s

kinda scary how much worse webview2 is... or maybe WKWebView is just too fast?

I wonder if webview2's custom uri scheme (which only works on win10+ :/ ) is more optimized for this :thinking: Not that it would matter for us until we drop support for 7&8 :sweat_smile: 
Edit: Nevermind, it works differently than on macos/linux and it will keep using the same webresourcerequested event we already use.

Also, the measurement includes reading the file from disk right? Maybe windows is just really bad at that part too

The file is included in the app with include_bytes!

Android performance is in the 700-800ms range.
iOS 70-100ms.
This PR is now ready, though we need a new wry release to publish.
wry 0.29 is published! You could update the dep to it.
So my question right out of the gate is: Why is this not implemented in wry directly?

> So my question right out of the gate is: Why is this not implemented in wry directly?

we actually need both the current IPC (postMessage) and custom protocol IPC.. wry already gives us the tools we need to so need to interfere there. Since wry is low level I don't think we should get this mess over there like handling Linux/Android/webkit2gtk-2.40 stuff.

Having lurked in this thread since the PR was first made I'm quite delighted to see this merged! I have been using the alpha releases for a while now and wonder how I would go about using this new feature together with the new v2 api plugins? 

Naively switching over the tauri and tauri-build dependencies to use the dev branch of course creates version conflicts with the fs plugin that I use. From where should I pull in the plugins?

> Naively switching over the tauri and tauri-build dependencies to use the dev branch of course creates version conflicts with the fs plugin that I use. From where should I pull in the plugins?

The v2 branch of plugins-workspace repo https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/tree/v2 or from the published crates on crates.io
but probably you should wait for the next alpha release (soon to be released).
On MacOS this breaks IPC using Remote Domains. Safari blocks the requests to localhost from other domains.

issue_context.title: [bug] naming an argument `cmd` causes unexpected and undocumented error
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

I named an argument for a custom command `cmd`, which used to work previously but now it seems to be a special name that gets treated differently by tauri. In fact it seems to override the command specified as the first parameter to `invoke()`.

```rust
#[tauri::command]
pub fn my_command(
  cmd: String
) -> Result<String, String> {
    info!("This never gets logged");
    Ok(String::new())
}
```
I invoked it from JS like this:
```
window.__TAURI__.invoke("my_command", {cmd: "test"})
```
and instead of calling my_command and passing that argument, it returns the error message `command "test" not found` in the frontend and the backend command was never executed.

This seems really strange to me. Why would certain argument names be considered special?
Is this documented anywhere?

Given that there are such special argument names, could these please be documented here? or at least somewhere prominent?
https://tauri.app/v1/guides/features/command

Even better, I'd argue that any "special" args internal to tauri should be an optional 3rd parameter to invoke() rather than overloading the user-supplied args list.

### Reproduction

```rust
#[tauri::command]
pub fn my_command(
  cmd: String
) -> Result<String, String> {
    info!("This never gets logged");
    Ok(String::new())
}
```

Now try to invoke the above command. This doesn't work:
```
window.__TAURI__.invoke("my_command", {cmd: "test"})
```
Instead it gives the error `Uncaught command test not found`

### Expected behavior

I'd expect all of the arguments given in the 2nd parameter to `invoke()` to be delivered to my function regardless, and not to have any "magic" args that are treated differently. Any such special internal args should be in a separate parameter given to `invoke()`

### Platform and versions

Environment
  › OS: Windows 10.0.22000 X64
  › Webview2: 103.0.1264.77
  › MSVC:
  › Node.js: 16.13.0
  › npm: 8.1.0
  › pnpm: Not installed!
  › yarn: Not installed!
  › rustup: 1.25.1
  › rustc: 1.62.0
  › cargo: 1.62.0
  › Rust toolchain: stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

### Stack trace

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_
comments:
Is it not fix in version   ` "@tauri-apps/api": "^1.1.0"` ? I encountered this bug when call a functhion like this:

```

#[tauri::command]
fn mycmd(cmd: &str) -> String{
    format!("Hello, {}! You've been greeted from Rust!", cmd)
}
```

> Is it not fix in version `"@tauri-apps/api": "^1.1.0"` ?

No, we can't fix this in a 1.X release because if people don't update the js _and_ rust packages _at the same time_, every js<->rust communication would break so we have to wait for v2 to fix it :/

review_comments: is there a reason we are using strings as errors instead of known enums? is this something we are planning to keep or refactor before v2

this is just the first layer of validation on the IPC request handler, it shouldn't fail in most cases (mostly if you request without using the `__TAURI__.invoke` helper). There's no need to have an enum here IMO.

IMHO if there are no secrets meant to be sent via headers it is totally fine as default.
In the default case there are only the `Content-Type`, `Tauri-Callback`, `Tauri-Error`, `Tauri-Channel-Id` header set. These are not containing secret values from my perspective. Leaking the `Tauri-Channel-Id` could be abused but I can not really think of a scenario where it could be leaked without already having more privileges.

If there are going to be secrets in the headers or cookies attached to the request the developer would need to modify the `ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_HEADERS` to suit their usage as the `*` value will be treated as a header name instead of a wildcard.

Can the developer modify this value at runtime or via configuration?
It doesn't seem supported on webkit https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Access-Control-Allow-Headers#browser_compatibility
we can add an API in Rust for this @tillmann-crabnebula though I'd wait for it to be requested actually.
I think we can turn this back into a match statement. I'll submit a change
Since the value is manually implemented instead of derived, we cannot use the constant as the pattern
